## Claim guides

### Claims against Abanca: floor clauses, mortgage costs and cards
URL: https://jurimatch.com/claims/abanca

Abanca is a Galician bank formed from the savings banks Caixa Galicia and Caixanova (later NCG Banco), which was among the banks in the case where the Spanish Supreme Court first ruled on floor clauses in May 2013. It now answers claims about NCG and the former savings banks' products.

Floor clauses (cláusulas suelo): Mortgage terms that set a minimum interest rate. Since 2013 Spanish courts have held them void where they were not transparent, and since the CJEU's December 2016 ruling banks must repay everything charged under a void clause, with interest.

Mortgage set-up costs (gastos de hipoteca): Customers have claimed back part of the notary, registry, agency and valuation costs charged when the mortgage was signed, after courts held clauses passing all costs to the customer to be unfair.

Revolving credit cards: Claims that the interest rate was usurious or that the cost of the card was not explained clearly. The Supreme Court has ruled on how to compare revolving rates with the market average.

IRPH-indexed mortgages: Claims about mortgages indexed to IRPH instead of Euribor, where the question is whether the bank explained the index and its effect transparently.

Former NCG preference shares: Customers who bought preference shares (preferentes) and subordinated debt from the Galician savings banks brought mis-selling claims, and many were offered arbitration or settlements. Check what you signed before starting a new claim.

Deadlines: In Spain, the Supreme Court and the Court of Justice of the European Union (CJEU) have held that the action to declare an unfair term void in a consumer contract does not expire. The time limit to recover money already paid is more debated: the CJEU has said it cannot start running before the consumer could know the term was unfair. Deadlines differ by product and are still developing through case law, so do not wait: get documents together and take advice early. Indicative period in Spain (contract claims): 5 years.

Sources:
- CJEU, Gutiérrez Naranjo, joined cases C-154/15, C-307/15 and C-308/15: https://curia.europa.eu/juris/liste.jsf?num=C-154/15
- CJEU, Gómez del Moral Guasch, case C-125/18 (IRPH): https://curia.europa.eu/juris/liste.jsf?num=C-125/18
- CJEU, CaixaBank and BBVA, cases C-224/19 and C-259/19 (mortgage costs): https://curia.europa.eu/juris/liste.jsf?num=C-224/19
- Banco de España: Portal del Cliente Bancario: https://clientebancario.bde.es/

Q: Do I have to complain to Abanca before going to court?
A: In practice, yes. A written complaint to the bank's customer service is required before you can go to the Banco de España complaints service, and since April 2025 most civil claims in Spain require a prior attempt to settle. A documented written complaint usually serves both purposes.

Q: Do lawyers take these cases on a no-win-no-fee basis?
A: Many do, especially floor clause and mortgage expense claims, because when the bank loses in full it is normally ordered to pay costs. Ask for the fee agreement (hoja de encargo) in writing, including what happens if the bank settles early.

Q: Can I still claim if I have paid off the loan?
A: Often yes. Having repaid or cancelled a mortgage does not by itself prevent a claim about an unfair term, but any later agreement or waiver you signed needs to be reviewed.

### Claims against Aer Lingus: delays, cancellations and refunds
URL: https://jurimatch.com/claims/aer-lingus

Aer Lingus is an Irish airline and part of International Airlines Group (IAG). Its flights are covered by Regulation 261/2004 when they depart from the EU or fly into the EU, and flights from the UK by UK261. Claims are mostly about cancellations, delays on transatlantic routes, refunds and baggage.

Delay and cancellation compensation: Under EU Regulation 261/2004 (and its UK copy, UK261), passengers can claim fixed compensation for long delays at arrival, late cancellations and denied boarding, unless the airline shows the disruption was caused by extraordinary circumstances such as severe weather or air traffic control restrictions. The amount depends on the flight distance.

Refunds and care: When a flight is cancelled, passengers are entitled to choose between a refund and re-routing, and to care (meals, and a hotel if an overnight stay is needed) while they wait. Customers have brought complaints where refunds were slow or only vouchers were offered.

Baggage: Lost, delayed or damaged luggage is covered by the Montreal Convention, which has short notice periods: report it at the airport and send a written claim to the airline quickly.

Deadlines: There is no single EU deadline for flight compensation: the limitation period is set by the law of the country where you bring the claim, and it varies considerably between countries. Baggage claims under the Montreal Convention have much shorter notice periods (days, not years) and a two-year limit for court action. Use the limitation checker for an indicative deadline in your country, and act early: evidence such as boarding passes and emails is easier to gather now. Indicative period in Ireland (contract claims): 6 years.

Sources:
- Regulation (EC) No 261/2004 (EUR-Lex): https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2004/261/oj
- UK261: Regulation 261/2004 as retained in UK law (legislation.gov.uk): https://www.legislation.gov.uk/eur/2004/261/contents
- European Commission: national enforcement bodies under Regulation 261/2004: https://transport.ec.europa.eu/transport-themes/passenger-rights/national-enforcement-bodies-neb_en

Q: Do I need a lawyer to claim compensation from Aer Lingus?
A: Usually not for the first step: you can claim directly with the airline for free. A claim company or no-win-no-fee lawyer can help if the airline refuses or does not reply, in exchange for a share of the compensation.

Q: Does Aer Lingus have to pay if the delay was caused by weather or strikes?
A: Not if the disruption was caused by extraordinary circumstances that could not have been avoided with reasonable measures, such as severe weather. Courts have held that strikes by the airline's own staff are not normally extraordinary, while strikes by third parties such as air traffic controllers can be. Each case depends on its facts.

Q: How much compensation can I get?
A: Under EU261 the fixed amounts are 250, 400 or 600 euros depending on distance (UK261 uses pounds). Our flight compensation calculator shows which band applies. Refunds and expenses for care are separate from compensation.

### Claims against Air Europa: delays, cancellations and refunds
URL: https://jurimatch.com/claims/air-europa

Air Europa is a Spanish airline based in Mallorca, with a hub in Madrid and many routes to Latin America. As an EU airline, its flights are covered by Regulation 261/2004 when they depart from the EU and when they fly into the EU, including flights from Latin America to Madrid.

Delay and cancellation compensation: Under EU Regulation 261/2004 (and its UK copy, UK261), passengers can claim fixed compensation for long delays at arrival, late cancellations and denied boarding, unless the airline shows the disruption was caused by extraordinary circumstances such as severe weather or air traffic control restrictions. The amount depends on the flight distance.

Baggage: Lost, delayed or damaged luggage is covered by the Montreal Convention, which has short notice periods: report it at the airport and send a written claim to the airline quickly.

Deadlines: There is no single EU deadline for flight compensation: the limitation period is set by the law of the country where you bring the claim, and it varies considerably between countries. Baggage claims under the Montreal Convention have much shorter notice periods (days, not years) and a two-year limit for court action. Use the limitation checker for an indicative deadline in your country, and act early: evidence such as boarding passes and emails is easier to gather now. Indicative period in Spain (contract claims): 5 years.

### Claims against Air France: delays, cancellations and refunds
URL: https://jurimatch.com/claims/air-france

Air France is France's flag carrier and part of the Air France-KLM group. As an EU airline, its flights are covered by Regulation 261/2004 when they depart from the EU and also when they fly into the EU from elsewhere. Claims are mostly about long delays, cancellations, missed connections on long-haul trips and refunds.

Delay and cancellation compensation: Under EU Regulation 261/2004 (and its UK copy, UK261), passengers can claim fixed compensation for long delays at arrival, late cancellations and denied boarding, unless the airline shows the disruption was caused by extraordinary circumstances such as severe weather or air traffic control restrictions. The amount depends on the flight distance.

Refunds and care: When a flight is cancelled, passengers are entitled to choose between a refund and re-routing, and to care (meals, and a hotel if an overnight stay is needed) while they wait. Customers have brought complaints where refunds were slow or only vouchers were offered.

Baggage: Lost, delayed or damaged luggage is covered by the Montreal Convention, which has short notice periods: report it at the airport and send a written claim to the airline quickly.

Deadlines: There is no single EU deadline for flight compensation: the limitation period is set by the law of the country where you bring the claim, and it varies considerably between countries. Baggage claims under the Montreal Convention have much shorter notice periods (days, not years) and a two-year limit for court action. Use the limitation checker for an indicative deadline in your country, and act early: evidence such as boarding passes and emails is easier to gather now. Indicative period in France (contract claims): 5 years (from knowledge).

Sources:

### Claims against Austrian Airlines: delays, cancellations and refunds
URL: https://jurimatch.com/claims/austrian-airlines

Austrian Airlines is Austria's national airline and part of the Lufthansa Group, with its hub in Vienna. Its flights are covered by Regulation 261/2004 when they depart from the EU or fly into the EU. Claims are mostly about delays, missed connections through Vienna, cancellations and refunds.

Delay and cancellation compensation: Under EU Regulation 261/2004 (and its UK copy, UK261), passengers can claim fixed compensation for long delays at arrival, late cancellations and denied boarding, unless the airline shows the disruption was caused by extraordinary circumstances such as severe weather or air traffic control restrictions. The amount depends on the flight distance.

Baggage claims under the Montreal Convention have much shorter notice periods (days, not years) and a two-year limit for court action. Use the limitation checker for an indicative deadline in your country, and act early: evidence such as boarding passes and emails is easier to gather now. Indicative period in Austria (contract claims): 3–30 years.

### Claims against Banco Sabadell: floor clauses, mortgage costs and cards
URL: https://jurimatch.com/claims/banco-sabadell

Banco Sabadell is one of Spain's largest banks and took over Caja de Ahorros del Mediterráneo (CAM) in 2012, so it now answers many claims about CAM mortgages and products. Like other Spanish banks, it has faced consumer claims over mortgage terms and credit products.

Floor clauses (cláusulas suelo): Mortgage terms that set a minimum interest rate. Since 2013 Spanish courts have held them void where they were not transparent, and since the CJEU's December 2016 ruling banks must repay everything charged under a void clause, with interest.

Mortgage set-up costs (gastos de hipoteca): Customers have claimed back part of the notary, registry, agency and valuation costs charged when the mortgage was signed, after courts held clauses passing all costs to the customer to be unfair.

Revolving credit cards: Claims that the interest rate was usurious or that the cost of the card was not explained clearly. The Supreme Court has ruled on how to compare revolving rates with the market average.

IRPH-indexed mortgages: Claims about mortgages indexed to IRPH instead of Euribor, where the question is whether the bank explained the index and its effect transparently.

Former CAM products: Holders of CAM preference shares (cuotas participativas, preferentes) and subordinated debt brought mis-selling claims after the savings bank was rescued. Outcomes depended on how and when the product was sold.

Deadlines: In Spain, the Supreme Court and the Court of Justice of the European Union (CJEU) have held that the action to declare an unfair term void in a consumer contract does not expire. The time limit to recover money already paid is more debated: the CJEU has said it cannot start running before the consumer could know the term was unfair. Deadlines differ by product and are still developing through case law, so do not wait: get documents together and take advice early. Indicative period in Spain (contract claims): 5 years.

Sources:
- CJEU, Gutiérrez Naranjo, joined cases C-154/15, C-307/15 and C-308/15: https://curia.europa.eu/juris/liste.jsf?num=C-154/15
- CJEU, Gómez del Moral Guasch, case C-125/18 (IRPH): https://curia.europa.eu/juris/liste.jsf?num=C-125/18
- CJEU, CaixaBank and BBVA, cases C-224/19 and C-259/19 (mortgage costs): https://curia.europa.eu/juris/liste.jsf?num=C-224/19
- Banco de España: Portal del Cliente Bancario: https://clientebancario.bde.es/

Q: Do I have to complain to Banco Sabadell before going to court?
A: In practice, yes. A written complaint to the bank's customer service is required before you can go to the Banco de España complaints service, and since April 2025 most civil claims in Spain require a prior attempt to settle. A documented written complaint usually serves both purposes.

Q: Do lawyers take these cases on a no-win-no-fee basis?
A: Many do, especially floor clause and mortgage expense claims, because when the bank loses in full it is normally ordered to pay costs. Ask for the fee agreement (hoja de encargo) in writing, including what happens if the bank settles early.

Q: Can I still claim if I have paid off the loan?
A: Often yes. Having repaid or cancelled a mortgage does not by itself prevent a claim about an unfair term, but any later agreement or waiver you signed needs to be reviewed.

### Claims against Bank Millennium: Swiss franc mortgages
URL: https://jurimatch.com/claims/bank-millennium

Bank Millennium is a Polish bank majority-owned by Portugal's Millennium bcp. It sold Swiss franc indexed mortgages and has faced many borrower claims about the exchange-rate clauses, and it has offered settlements to convert loans into zlotys.

Swiss franc mortgages (kredyty frankowe): Borrowers with mortgages indexed to or denominated in Swiss francs have claimed that the exchange-rate clauses were unfair because the bank set the rate and did not explain the currency risk. In Dziubak (C-260/18, October 2019) the Court of Justice of the EU held that a court may annul the whole contract where it cannot continue without the unfair term.

What happens if the contract is annulled: Both sides return what they received: the borrower the capital, the bank the instalments. In June 2023 (C-520/21) the CJEU held that EU law precludes the bank from claiming remuneration beyond the capital it lent, and Polish courts have since applied that ruling.

Settlements offered by banks: Several banks have offered settlements converting the loan into zlotys. A settlement can end the dispute, so compare it with the likely result of a court case before signing.

Deadlines: In Poland, claims by consumers are generally subject to a six-year limitation period that ends on the last day of the calendar year. For Swiss franc loans, courts have held that the period for the borrower runs from when the borrower knew, or should have known, that the clause was unfair. Deadlines in these cases are still argued in court, so do not wait: gather the loan documents and get advice early. Indicative period in Poland (contract claims): 3–6 years.

Sources:
- CJEU, Dziubak, case C-260/18: https://curia.europa.eu/juris/liste.jsf?num=C-260/18
- CJEU, Bank M., case C-520/21: https://curia.europa.eu/juris/liste.jsf?num=C-520/21
- Rzecznik Finansowy (Polish Financial Ombudsman): https://rf.gov.pl/

Q: Can I still sue Bank Millennium if I have repaid the Swiss franc loan?
A: Often yes. Borrowers who have repaid their loan have brought claims to recover what they overpaid, but the deadline question needs checking for your dates.

Q: Do lawyers take these cases on a success fee?
A: Many Polish firms offer a fixed fee plus a success fee, or a success fee only. Ask for the agreement in writing and how the fee is calculated if the bank settles.

Q: What did the CJEU decide about bank remuneration?
A: In June 2023 (case C-520/21) the Court held that, when a loan contract is annulled because of unfair terms, EU law precludes the bank from claiming compensation beyond the return of the capital and interest on it from when the payment was demanded.

### Claims against Bankinter: floor clauses, mortgage costs and cards
URL: https://jurimatch.com/claims/bankinter

Bankinter is a Spanish bank known for its mortgage and private banking business. Besides the mortgage terms common to Spanish banks, customers have brought claims over multi-currency mortgages (hipotecas multidivisa) linked to foreign currencies such as the Swiss franc or the yen. This guide explains the usual claims and routes in Spain.

Floor clauses (cláusulas suelo): Mortgage terms that set a minimum interest rate. Since 2013 Spanish courts have held them void where they were not transparent, and since the CJEU's December 2016 ruling banks must repay everything charged under a void clause, with interest.

Mortgage set-up costs (gastos de hipoteca): Customers have claimed back part of the notary, registry, agency and valuation costs charged when the mortgage was signed, after courts held clauses passing all costs to the customer to be unfair.

Revolving credit cards: Claims that the interest rate was usurious or that the cost of the card was not explained clearly. The Supreme Court has ruled on how to compare revolving rates with the market average.

IRPH-indexed mortgages: Claims about mortgages indexed to IRPH instead of Euribor, where the question is whether the bank explained the index and its effect transparently.

Multi-currency mortgages: Mortgages repaid in or indexed to a foreign currency. Customers have claimed that the currency risk was not explained clearly; Spanish courts have annulled the currency clause where the bank could not show it gave enough information.

Deadlines: In Spain, the Supreme Court and the Court of Justice of the European Union (CJEU) have held that the action to declare an unfair term void in a consumer contract does not expire. The time limit to recover money already paid is more debated: the CJEU has said it cannot start running before the consumer could know the term was unfair. Deadlines differ by product and are still developing through case law, so do not wait: get documents together and take advice early. Indicative period in Spain (contract claims): 5 years.

Sources:
- CJEU, Gutiérrez Naranjo, joined cases C-154/15, C-307/15 and C-308/15: https://curia.europa.eu/juris/liste.jsf?num=C-154/15
- CJEU, Gómez del Moral Guasch, case C-125/18 (IRPH): https://curia.europa.eu/juris/liste.jsf?num=C-125/18
- CJEU, CaixaBank and BBVA, cases C-224/19 and C-259/19 (mortgage costs): https://curia.europa.eu/juris/liste.jsf?num=C-224/19
- Banco de España: Portal del Cliente Bancario: https://clientebancario.bde.es/

Q: Do I have to complain to Bankinter before going to court?
A: In practice, yes. A written complaint to the bank's customer service is required before you can go to the Banco de España complaints service, and since April 2025 most civil claims in Spain require a prior attempt to settle. A documented written complaint usually serves both purposes.

Q: Do lawyers take these cases on a no-win-no-fee basis?
A: Many do, especially floor clause and mortgage expense claims, because when the bank loses in full it is normally ordered to pay costs. Ask for the fee agreement (hoja de encargo) in writing, including what happens if the bank settles early.

Q: Can I still claim if I have paid off the loan?
A: Often yes. Having repaid or cancelled a mortgage does not by itself prevent a claim about an unfair term, but any later agreement or waiver you signed needs to be reviewed.

### Claims against BBVA: floor clauses, mortgage costs and cards
URL: https://jurimatch.com/claims/bbva

BBVA is one of Spain's largest banks. It was among the banks in the case in which the Spanish Supreme Court first ruled on floor clauses in May 2013, and like other Spanish banks it has faced consumer claims over mortgage terms and credit products. This guide explains the usual claims and routes in Spain.

Floor clauses (cláusulas suelo): Mortgage terms that set a minimum interest rate. Since 2013 Spanish courts have held them void where they were not transparent, and since the CJEU's December 2016 ruling banks must repay everything charged under a void clause, with interest.

Mortgage set-up costs (gastos de hipoteca): Customers have claimed back part of the notary, registry, agency and valuation costs charged when the mortgage was signed, after courts held clauses passing all costs to the customer to be unfair.

Revolving credit cards: Claims that the interest rate was usurious or that the cost of the card was not explained clearly. The Supreme Court has ruled on how to compare revolving rates with the market average.

IRPH-indexed mortgages: Claims about mortgages indexed to IRPH instead of Euribor, where the question is whether the bank explained the index and its effect transparently.

Deadlines differ by product and are still developing through case law, so do not wait: get documents together and take advice early. Indicative period in Spain (contract claims): 5 years.

- CJEU, CaixaBank and BBVA, cases C-224/19 and C-259/19 (mortgage costs): https://curia.europa.eu/juris/liste.jsf?num=C-224/19
- Banco de España: Portal del Cliente Bancario: https://clientebancario.bde.es/

Q: Do I have to complain to BBVA before going to court?
A: In practice, yes. A written complaint to the bank's customer service is required before you can go to the Banco de España complaints service, and since April 2025 most civil claims in Spain require a prior attempt to settle. A documented written complaint usually serves both purposes.

Q: Do lawyers take these cases on a no-win-no-fee basis?

A: Often yes. Having repaid or cancelled a mortgage does not by itself prevent a claim about an unfair term, but any later agreement or waiver you signed needs to be reviewed.

### Claims against Booking.com: parity clauses and hotel claims
URL: https://jurimatch.com/claims/booking-com

Booking.com, based in Amsterdam, used price parity clauses that stopped hotels offering lower prices elsewhere. In September 2024 the Court of Justice of the EU ruled (case C-264/23) that such clauses are not, in principle, an ancillary restraint exempt from competition law. Hotels in several countries have since brought or announced damages claims.

Hotel damages claims: Hotels have claimed that parity clauses kept commissions and room prices higher than they would otherwise have been. The CJEU ruling answered questions referred by a Dutch court in a dispute brought by German hotels.

Group claims: Associations and funded claim vehicles have organised group claims for hotels in several European countries. Check their terms and the period they cover.

Deadlines: Limitation depends on the country where the claim is brought and on when the hotel knew of the infringement. Clauses differed by country and period (wide and narrow parity), so dates matter. Get the dates of your contract and of any clause changes checked early. Indicative period in the Netherlands (non-contractual damages (tort)): 5 years (from knowledge).

Sources:
- CJEU, Booking.com, case C-264/23 (parity clauses): https://curia.europa.eu/juris/liste.jsf?num=C-264/23
- Directive 2014/104/EU on competition damages actions (EUR-Lex): https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2014/104/oj

Q: Can guests claim against Booking.com for parity clauses?
A: The claims brought so far are by hotels, which paid the commissions. Guests' claims would be much harder to prove.

Q: Does the CJEU ruling decide the damages?
A: No. It answered questions of competition law; national courts decide whether there was an infringement in each case and how much damage it caused.

### Claims against British Airways: delays, cancellations and refunds
URL: https://jurimatch.com/claims/british-airways

British Airways is the UK's flag carrier and part of International Airlines Group (IAG). Flights from the UK, and BA flights into the UK, are covered by UK261, the UK copy of the EU rules with amounts in pounds; BA flights departing from the EU are covered by EU261. Claims are mostly about delays, cancellations, refunds and baggage.

Delay and cancellation compensation: Under EU Regulation 261/2004 (and its UK copy, UK261), passengers can claim fixed compensation for long delays at arrival, late cancellations and denied boarding, unless the airline shows the disruption was caused by extraordinary circumstances such as severe weather or air traffic control restrictions. The amount depends on the flight distance.

Refunds and care: When a flight is cancelled, passengers are entitled to choose between a refund and re-routing, and to care (meals, and a hotel if an overnight stay is needed) while they wait. Customers have brought complaints where refunds were slow or only vouchers were offered.

Baggage: Lost, delayed or damaged luggage is covered by the Montreal Convention, which has short notice periods: report it at the airport and send a written claim to the airline quickly.

Deadlines: There is no single EU deadline for flight compensation: the limitation period is set by the law of the country where you bring the claim, and it varies considerably between countries. Baggage claims under the Montreal Convention have much shorter notice periods (days, not years) and a two-year limit for court action. Use the limitation checker for an indicative deadline in your country, and act early: evidence such as boarding passes and emails is easier to gather now. Indicative period in the United Kingdom (contract claims): 6 years.

Sources:
- Regulation (EC) No 261/2004 (EUR-Lex): https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2004/261/oj
- UK261: Regulation 261/2004 as retained in UK law (legislation.gov.uk): https://www.legislation.gov.uk/eur/2004/261/contents
- European Commission: national enforcement bodies under Regulation 261/2004: https://transport.ec.europa.eu/transport-themes/passenger-rights/national-enforcement-bodies-neb_en

Q: Do I need a lawyer to claim compensation from British Airways?
A: Usually not for the first step: you can claim directly with the airline for free. A claim company or no-win-no-fee lawyer can help if the airline refuses or does not reply, in exchange for a share of the compensation.

Q: Does British Airways have to pay if the delay was caused by weather or strikes?
A: Not if the disruption was caused by extraordinary circumstances that could not have been avoided with reasonable measures, such as severe weather. Courts have held that strikes by the airline's own staff are not normally extraordinary, while strikes by third parties such as air traffic controllers can be. Each case depends on its facts.

Q: How much compensation can I get?
A: Under EU261 the fixed amounts are 250, 400 or 600 euros depending on distance (UK261 uses pounds). Our flight compensation calculator shows which band applies. Refunds and expenses for care are separate from compensation.

### Claims against Brussels Airlines: delays, cancellations and refunds
URL: https://jurimatch.com/claims/brussels-airlines

Brussels Airlines is Belgium's main airline and part of the Lufthansa Group, with its hub at Brussels Airport and many routes to Africa. Its flights are covered by Regulation 261/2004 when they depart from the EU or fly into the EU.

### When a business partner takes the money: your options
URL: https://jurimatch.com/claims/business-partner-fraud

Partnership and shareholder disputes often start with exclusion from information and end with diverted revenue, dilution or asset stripping. Acting early protects both evidence and value.

Q: Can a shareholder dispute be funded?
A: Yes, where the business or stake is valuable enough. Funders and success-fee firms look at what can realistically be recovered or bought out.

### Claims against CaixaBank: mortgages, cards and former Bankia
URL: https://jurimatch.com/claims/caixabank

CaixaBank is one of Spain's largest banks and absorbed Bankia in 2021, so it is now the counterparty for many claims that began against Bankia. Like other Spanish banks, it has faced consumer claims over mortgage terms and credit products. This guide explains the usual claims and routes in Spain.

Floor clauses (cláusulas suelo): Mortgage terms that set a minimum interest rate. Since 2013 Spanish courts have held them void where they were not transparent, and since the CJEU's December 2016 ruling banks must repay everything charged under a void clause, with interest.

Mortgage set-up costs (gastos de hipoteca): Customers have claimed back part of the notary, registry, agency and valuation costs charged when the mortgage was signed, after courts held clauses passing all costs to the customer to be unfair.

Revolving credit cards: Claims that the interest rate was usurious or that the cost of the card was not explained clearly. The Supreme Court has ruled on how to compare revolving rates with the market average.

IRPH-indexed mortgages: Claims about mortgages indexed to IRPH instead of Euribor, where the question is whether the bank explained the index and its effect transparently.

Former Bankia products: Retail investors brought claims over Bankia's 2011 stock market listing, and in 2016 the Supreme Court allowed retail buyers to annul their purchases because of serious inaccuracies in the prospectus. Holders of preference shares (preferentes) and subordinated debt sold by Bankia and the savings banks that formed it also brought mis-selling claims.

Deadlines: In Spain, the Supreme Court and the Court of Justice of the European Union (CJEU) have held that the action to declare an unfair term void in a consumer contract does not expire. The time limit to recover money already paid is more debated: the CJEU has said it cannot start running before the consumer could know the term was unfair. Deadlines differ by product and are still developing through case law, so do not wait: get documents together and take advice early. Indicative period in Spain (contract claims): 5 years.

Sources:
- CJEU, Gutiérrez Naranjo, joined cases C-154/15, C-307/15 and C-308/15: https://curia.europa.eu/juris/liste.jsf?num=C-154/15
- CJEU, CaixaBank and BBVA, cases C-224/19 and C-259/19 (mortgage costs): https://curia.europa.eu/juris/liste.jsf?num=C-224/19
- Banco de España: Portal del Cliente Bancario: https://clientebancario.bde.es/

Q: Do I have to complain to CaixaBank before going to court?
A: In practice, yes. A written complaint to the bank's customer service is required before you can go to the Banco de España complaints service, and since April 2025 most civil claims in Spain require a prior attempt to settle. A documented written complaint usually serves both purposes.

Q: Do lawyers take these cases on a no-win-no-fee basis?
A: Many do, especially floor clause and mortgage expense claims, because when the bank loses in full it is normally ordered to pay costs. Ask for the fee agreement (hoja de encargo) in writing, including what happens if the bank settles early.

A: Often yes. Having repaid or cancelled a mortgage does not by itself prevent a claim about an unfair term, but any later agreement or waiver you signed needs to be reviewed.

### Crypto scam recovery: first steps and how lawyers trace funds
URL: https://jurimatch.com/claims/crypto-scam

Crypto transfers are public on the blockchain, which means funds can sometimes be followed to an exchange where an account holder can be identified. Speed matters: once funds are moved through mixers or off-ramped, options narrow.

Q: Can stolen crypto be recovered?
A: Sometimes, if the funds can be traced to an exchange or custodian that can be compelled to freeze and disclose account information. If funds were moved through mixers or to wallets nobody controls identifiably, recovery is much harder.

Q: Is there a no-win-no-fee option for crypto fraud?
A: Some firms work on success terms when tracing shows funds at an identifiable exchange. Initial tracing reports often carry a cost, so ask upfront what is included.

Q: How do I spot a recovery scam?
A: Unsolicited contact, upfront fees, claims of special access to blockchains or regulators, and pressure to act fast. Legitimate law firms are regulated and can be checked with the local bar or law society.

### Claims against DAF Trucks: the trucks cartel
URL: https://jurimatch.com/claims/daf-trucks

DAF, the Dutch truck maker owned by PACCAR, was fined by the European Commission in July 2016 for the trucks cartel. DAF buyers have brought many of the leading cases, including the Spanish case that reached the CJEU in 2022.

Damages for overcharges: In July 2016 the European Commission found that MAN, Volvo/Renault, Daimler, Iveco and DAF had colluded for 14 years (1997 to 2011) on truck pricing and on passing on the costs of emissions technology, and in September 2017 it found the same about Scania. Buyers and lessees of medium and heavy trucks from that period have claimed the extra price they paid.

Group claims: Many hauliers have joined group claims organised by law firms, associations or claim vehicles, often backed by litigation funders, in Spain, Germany, the Netherlands, the United Kingdom and elsewhere.

How the overcharge is proved: Claims rely on expert economic reports comparing cartel prices with the prices that would have applied without the cartel. Courts in several countries have estimated the damage when the evidence was incomplete.

Deadlines: In Volvo and DAF Trucks (C-267/20, June 2022) the CJEU held that the limitation period for these claims could not start before the Commission's decision was published in the EU Official Journal (April 2017 for the main decision), and applied the rules of the Damages Directive to many claims. Each country's limitation rules then apply, and some claims are already out of time. Check your dates with a lawyer before assuming your claim is open. Indicative period in the Netherlands (non-contractual damages (tort)): 5 years (from knowledge).

Sources:
- European Commission: trucks cartel decision, July 2016: https://ec.europa.eu/commission/presscorner/detail/en/IP_16_2582
- CJEU, Volvo and DAF Trucks, case C-267/20 (limitation of cartel claims): https://curia.europa.eu/juris/liste.jsf?num=C-267/20
- Directive 2014/104/EU on competition damages actions (EUR-Lex): https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2014/104/oj

Q: Can my company still claim against DAF Trucks?
A: Possibly, depending on the country where you sue and when your limitation period started. After the CJEU's 2022 ruling many claims were filed, but each country's own rules decide whether yours is still open.

Q: Do I need the original invoices?
A: They help a lot. Where they are lost, registration records and bank statements can sometimes prove the purchase and its price.

Q: Who pays the expert report?
A: In group claims the funder or the law firm usually advances it and recovers it from the proceeds. In an individual claim, ask the firm how it is paid.

### Claims against Daimler Truck: the trucks cartel
URL: https://jurimatch.com/claims/daimler-truck

Daimler Truck, the German maker of Mercedes-Benz trucks, was one of the manufacturers fined by the European Commission in July 2016 for the trucks cartel. Buyers of its trucks from 1997 to 2011 have claimed damages for the overcharge, alone or in group claims.

Damages for overcharges: In July 2016 the European Commission found that MAN, Volvo/Renault, Daimler, Iveco and DAF had colluded for 14 years (1997 to 2011) on truck pricing and on passing on the costs of emissions technology, and in September 2017 it found the same about Scania. Indicative period in Germany (non-contractual damages (tort)): 3 years (from knowledge).

### Claims against Deutsche Bahn: train delays and refunds
URL: https://jurimatch.com/claims/deutsche-bahn

Deutsche Bahn is Germany's national rail operator. Its long-distance and regional trains are covered by the EU rail passenger rights rules, and German law adds some rights for local transport. Claims are mostly about delays, missed connections and cancelled trains.

Delay compensation: Under Regulation (EU) 2021/782, which applies since June 2023, passengers can claim 25% of the ticket price for a delay at arrival of 60 to 119 minutes and 50% for 120 minutes or more, unless the delay was caused by extraordinary circumstances such as severe weather. Operators can set a minimum amount below which nothing is paid.

Refund or re-routing: If a delay of 60 minutes or more is expected, passengers can choose a refund, continuing the journey or re-routing, and are entitled to meals and, where needed, a hotel.

Deadlines: Regulation 2021/782 lets operators set a time limit for compensation requests, which cannot be shorter than three months after the journey. Ask for compensation as soon as possible. A court claim after that is subject to the general limitation rules of the country where you sue. Indicative period in Germany (contract claims): 3 years (from knowledge).

Sources:
- Regulation (EU) 2021/782 on rail passengers' rights (EUR-Lex): https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2021/782/oj

Q: How much does Deutsche Bahn pay for a delay?
A: Under the EU minimum rules, 25% of the ticket price for 60 to 119 minutes late and 50% for 120 minutes or more. Some operators pay more under their own commitments; check the conditions of your ticket.

Q: Is a strike an extraordinary circumstance?
A: Regulation 2021/782 lists exceptions such as extreme weather and major natural disasters; strikes by the operator's own staff are not among them. Check the facts of your case.

### Claims against easyJet: delays, cancellations and refunds
URL: https://jurimatch.com/claims/easyjet

easyJet operates through a UK company and separate European companies, so a flight can fall under the EU rules (EU261) or the UK rules (UK261) depending on the route and the operating carrier. Passenger claims are mostly about long delays, cancellations, refunds and baggage.

Delay and cancellation compensation: Under EU Regulation 261/2004 (and its UK copy, UK261), passengers can claim fixed compensation for long delays at arrival, late cancellations and denied boarding, unless the airline shows the disruption was caused by extraordinary circumstances such as severe weather or air traffic control restrictions. The amount depends on the flight distance.

EU261 or UK261?: Flights departing from the UK are covered by UK261; flights departing from the EU, or arriving in the EU on an EU-licensed airline, by EU261. Your boarding pass or booking shows which easyJet company operated the flight.

Refunds and care: When a flight is cancelled, passengers are entitled to choose between a refund and re-routing, and to care (meals, and a hotel if an overnight stay is needed) while they wait. Customers have brought complaints where refunds were slow or only vouchers were offered.

Baggage: Lost, delayed or damaged luggage is covered by the Montreal Convention, which has short notice periods: report it at the airport and send a written claim to the airline quickly.

Deadlines: There is no single EU deadline for flight compensation: the limitation period is set by the law of the country where you bring the claim, and it varies considerably between countries. Baggage claims under the Montreal Convention have much shorter notice periods (days, not years) and a two-year limit for court action. Use the limitation checker for an indicative deadline in your country, and act early: evidence such as boarding passes and emails is easier to gather now. Indicative period in the United Kingdom (contract claims): 6 years.

Sources:
- UK261: Regulation 261/2004 as retained in UK law (legislation.gov.uk): https://www.legislation.gov.uk/eur/2004/261/contents
- Regulation (EC) No 261/2004 (EUR-Lex): https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2004/261/oj

Q: Does easyJet have to pay if the delay was caused by weather or strikes?
A: Not if the disruption was caused by extraordinary circumstances that could not have been avoided with reasonable measures, such as severe weather. Courts have held that strikes by the airline's own staff are not normally extraordinary, while strikes by third parties such as air traffic controllers can be. Each case depends on its facts.

Q: How much compensation can I get?
A: Under EU261 the fixed amounts are 250, 400 or 600 euros depending on distance (UK261 uses pounds). Our flight compensation calculator shows which band applies. Refunds and expenses for care are separate from compensation.

A: Under EU261 the fixed amounts are 250, 400 or 600 euros depending on distance (UK261 uses pounds). Our flight compensation calculator shows which band applies. Refunds and expenses for care are separate from compensation.

### Claims against Google: competition damages (Google Shopping)
URL: https://jurimatch.com/claims/google

In June 2017 the European Commission fined Google for favouring its own comparison shopping service in search results. The General Court upheld the decision in 2021 and the Court of Justice of the EU dismissed Google's final appeal in September 2024 (case C-48/22 P). Price comparison sites and other businesses have since claimed damages in national courts.

Comparison shopping services: Businesses that ran comparison shopping sites in Europe have claimed lost profits caused by Google's conduct. A final infringement decision binds national courts, so these follow-on claims focus on the damage and its amount.

Advertisers and other businesses: Group claims have also been brought on behalf of advertisers and other business users, arguing that Google's conduct raised prices. Whether they succeed depends on proving the harm.

Deadlines: Under the Damages Directive the limitation period is at least five years and cannot start before the infringement ended and the claimant knew of it; national rules on when it starts differ. The final CJEU judgment of September 2024 is relevant to when time runs in many countries, so check the dates with a lawyer.

Sources:
- CJEU, Google and Alphabet v Commission, case C-48/22 P (Google Shopping): https://curia.europa.eu/juris/liste.jsf?num=C-48/22
- Directive 2014/104/EU on competition damages actions (EUR-Lex): https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2014/104/oj

Q: Do I have to prove that Google broke competition law?
A: Not for the conduct covered by a final Commission decision: national courts are bound by it. You still have to prove the damage you suffered and its link to the infringement.

Q: Are these claims funded?
A: Often. Litigation funders back many competition damages claims in exchange for a share of the recovery.

### Claims against Ibercaja: floor clauses, mortgage costs and cards
URL: https://jurimatch.com/claims/ibercaja

Ibercaja is a Spanish bank based in Zaragoza, created from a savings bank, which absorbed Caja3 in 2013. Like other Spanish banks, it has faced consumer claims over floor clauses, mortgage costs, IRPH-indexed mortgages and credit cards.

Floor clauses (cláusulas suelo): Mortgage terms that set a minimum interest rate. Since 2013 Spanish courts have held them void where they were not transparent, and since the CJEU's December 2016 ruling banks must repay everything charged under a void clause, with interest.

Mortgage set-up costs (gastos de hipoteca): Customers have claimed back part of the notary, registry, agency and valuation costs charged when the mortgage was signed, after courts held clauses passing all costs to the customer to be unfair.

Revolving credit cards: Claims that the interest rate was usurious or that the cost of the card was not explained clearly. The Supreme Court has ruled on how to compare revolving rates with the market average.

IRPH-indexed mortgages: Claims about mortgages indexed to IRPH instead of Euribor, where the question is whether the bank explained the index and its effect transparently.

Deadlines: In Spain, the Supreme Court and the Court of Justice of the European Union (CJEU) have held that the action to declare an unfair term void in a consumer contract does not expire. The time limit to recover money already paid is more debated: the CJEU has said it cannot start running before the consumer could know the term was unfair. Deadlines differ by product and are still developing through case law, so do not wait: get documents together and take advice early. Indicative period in Spain (contract claims): 5 years.

Sources:
- CJEU, Gutiérrez Naranjo, joined cases C-154/15, C-307/15 and C-308/15: https://curia.europa.eu/juris/liste.jsf?num=C-154/15
- CJEU, Gómez del Moral Guasch, case C-125/18 (IRPH): https://curia.europa.eu/juris/liste.jsf?num=C-125/18
- CJEU, CaixaBank and BBVA, cases C-224/19 and C-259/19 (mortgage costs): https://curia.europa.eu/juris/liste.jsf?num=C-224/19
- Banco de España: Portal del Cliente Bancario: https://clientebancario.bde.es/

Q: Do I have to complain to Ibercaja before going to court?
A: In practice, yes. A written complaint to the bank's customer service is required before you can go to the Banco de España complaints service, and since April 2025 most civil claims in Spain require a prior attempt to settle. A documented written complaint usually serves both purposes.

Q: Do lawyers take these cases on a no-win-no-fee basis?
A: Many do, especially floor clause and mortgage expense claims, because when the bank loses in full it is normally ordered to pay costs. Ask for the fee agreement (hoja de encargo) in writing, including what happens if the bank settles early.

Q: Can I still claim if I have paid off the loan?
A: Often yes. Having repaid or cancelled a mortgage does not by itself prevent a claim about an unfair term, but any later agreement or waiver you signed needs to be reviewed.

### Claims against Iberia: delays, cancellations and refunds
URL: https://jurimatch.com/claims/iberia

Iberia is a Spanish airline, so its flights are generally covered by EU Regulation 261/2004, including long-haul flights departing from Spain. Passenger claims are mostly about long delays, cancellations, missed connections, refunds and baggage.

Delay and cancellation compensation: Under EU Regulation 261/2004 (and its UK copy, UK261), passengers can claim fixed compensation for long delays at arrival, late cancellations and denied boarding, unless the airline shows the disruption was caused by extraordinary circumstances such as severe weather or air traffic control restrictions. The amount depends on the flight distance.

Missed connections: When connecting flights are booked together and you reach the final destination more than three hours late, compensation is generally calculated on the distance to the final destination.

Refunds and care: When a flight is cancelled, passengers are entitled to choose between a refund and re-routing, and to care (meals, and a hotel if an overnight stay is needed) while they wait. Customers have brought complaints where refunds were slow or only vouchers were offered.

Baggage: Lost, delayed or damaged luggage is covered by the Montreal Convention, which has short notice periods: report it at the airport and send a written claim to the airline quickly.

Deadlines: There is no single EU deadline for flight compensation: the limitation period is set by the law of the country where you bring the claim, and it varies considerably between countries. Baggage claims under the Montreal Convention have much shorter notice periods (days, not years) and a two-year limit for court action. Use the limitation checker for an indicative deadline in your country, and act early: evidence such as boarding passes and emails is easier to gather now. Indicative period in Spain (contract claims): 5 years.

Sources:
- Regulation (EC) No 261/2004 (EUR-Lex): https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2004/261/oj
- European Commission: national enforcement bodies under Regulation 261/2004: https://transport.ec.europa.eu/transport-themes/passenger-rights/national-enforcement-bodies-neb_en

Q: Do I need a lawyer to claim compensation from Iberia?
A: Usually not for the first step: you can claim directly with the airline for free. A claim company or no-win-no-fee lawyer can help if the airline refuses or does not reply, in exchange for a share of the compensation.

Q: Does Iberia have to pay if the delay was caused by weather or strikes?
A: Not if the disruption was caused by extraordinary circumstances that could not have been avoided with reasonable measures, such as severe weather. Courts have held that strikes by the airline's own staff are not normally extraordinary, while strikes by third parties such as air traffic controllers can be. Each case depends on its facts.

Q: How much compensation can I get?
A: Under EU261 the fixed amounts are 250, 400 or 600 euros depending on distance (UK261 uses pounds). Our flight compensation calculator shows which band applies. Refunds and expenses for care are separate from compensation.

### Insurance claim denied? How to challenge it
URL: https://jurimatch.com/claims/insurance-claim-denied

Insurers reject claims for many reasons, exclusions, late notification, alleged non-disclosure or disputes about the value of the loss. Many rejections can be challenged.

Q: Do lawyers take insurance disputes on a no-win-no-fee basis?
A: Often, because the insurer can pay. The main question is whether the policy wording supports your claim.

### Lost money to investment fraud? What to do first
URL: https://jurimatch.com/claims/investment-fraud

Investment fraud covers Ponzi schemes, fake funds, unauthorised trading, mis-sold products and advisers who misrepresented risk. The steps you take in the first weeks often decide whether money can still be traced and recovered.

Q: Can I get my money back from an investment scam?
A: Sometimes. It depends on whether the money can be traced, whether a solvent party (a bank, a regulated firm or an identifiable individual with assets) is responsible, and how quickly you act. A lawyer can tell you which of these applies to you.

Q: Do lawyers take investment fraud cases on a no-win-no-fee basis?
A: Many do, where recovery looks realistic, for example when a regulated entity or insurer is involved, or many investors were affected by the same scheme. Where it is less certain, firms may offer a reduced fee plus a success fee, or refer you to a litigation funder.

Q: Should I join a group claim?
A: Group or collective actions can share costs and make funding easier. Check who runs the claim, how fees are taken from any recovery, and whether you can leave.

### Claims against ITA Airways: delays, cancellations and refunds
URL: https://jurimatch.com/claims/ita-airways

ITA Airways is the Italian airline that started flying in October 2021, when Alitalia stopped operating. It is a separate company from Alitalia, so claims about earlier Alitalia flights are not normally brought against ITA. Its flights are covered by Regulation 261/2004 when they depart from or fly into the EU.

Use the limitation checker for an indicative deadline in your country, and act early: evidence such as boarding passes and emails is easier to gather now. Indicative period in Italy (contract claims): 10 years.

### Claims against Iveco: the trucks cartel
URL: https://jurimatch.com/claims/iveco

Iveco, the Italian truck maker, was fined by the European Commission in July 2016 for the trucks cartel. Buyers of Iveco trucks from 1997 to 2011 have claimed damages for the overcharge in Italy, Spain and other countries.

Damages for overcharges: In July 2016 the European Commission found that MAN, Volvo/Renault, Daimler, Iveco and DAF had colluded for 14 years (1997 to 2011) on truck pricing and on passing on the costs of emissions technology, and in September 2017 it found the same about Scania. Buyers and lessees of medium and heavy trucks from that period have claimed the extra price they paid.

Group claims: Many hauliers have joined group claims organised by law firms, associations or claim vehicles, often backed by litigation funders, in Spain, Germany, the Netherlands, the United Kingdom and elsewhere.

How the overcharge is proved: Claims rely on expert economic reports comparing cartel prices with the prices that would have applied without the cartel. Courts in several countries have estimated the damage when the evidence was incomplete.

Deadlines: In Volvo and DAF Trucks (C-267/20, June 2022) the CJEU held that the limitation period for these claims could not start before the Commission's decision was published in the EU Official Journal (April 2017 for the main decision), and applied the rules of the Damages Directive to many claims. Each country's limitation rules then apply, and some claims are already out of time. Check your dates with a lawyer before assuming your claim is open. Indicative period in Italy (non-contractual damages (tort)): 5 years (from knowledge).

Sources:
- European Commission: trucks cartel decision, July 2016: https://ec.europa.eu/commission/presscorner/detail/en/IP_16_2582
- CJEU, Volvo and DAF Trucks, case C-267/20 (limitation of cartel claims): https://curia.europa.eu/juris/liste.jsf?num=C-267/20
- Directive 2014/104/EU on competition damages actions (EUR-Lex): https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2014/104/oj

Q: Can my company still claim against Iveco?
A: Possibly, depending on the country where you sue and when your limitation period started. After the CJEU's 2022 ruling many claims were filed, but each country's own rules decide whether yours is still open.

Q: Do I need the original invoices?
A: They help a lot. Where they are lost, registration records and bank statements can sometimes prove the purchase and its price.

Q: Who pays the expert report?
A: In group claims the funder or the law firm usually advances it and recovers it from the proceeds. In an individual claim, ask the firm how it is paid.

URL: https://jurimatch.com/claims/lufthansa

Lufthansa is a German airline, so its flights are generally covered by EU Regulation 261/2004, including long-haul flights departing from the EU. ### Claims against mBank: Swiss franc mortgages
URL: https://jurimatch.com/claims/mbank

mBank is a Polish bank majority-owned by Germany's Commerzbank. It sold mortgages indexed to the Swiss franc before the 2008 financial crisis and has faced a large number of claims from borrowers about the exchange-rate clauses.

Swiss franc mortgages (kredyty frankowe): Borrowers with mortgages indexed to or denominated in Swiss francs have claimed that the exchange-rate clauses were unfair because the bank set the rate and did not explain the currency risk. In Dziubak (C-260/18, October 2019) the Court of Justice of the EU held that a court may annul the whole contract where it cannot continue without the unfair term.

What happens if the contract is annulled: Both sides return what they received: the borrower the capital, the bank the instalments. In June 2023 (C-520/21) the CJEU held that EU law precludes the bank from claiming remuneration beyond the capital it lent, and Polish courts have since applied that ruling.

Settlements offered by banks: Several banks have offered settlements converting the loan into zlotys. A settlement can end the dispute, so compare it with the likely result of a court case before signing.

Deadlines: In Poland, claims by consumers are generally subject to a six-year limitation period that ends on the last day of the calendar year. For Swiss franc loans, courts have held that the period for the borrower runs from when the borrower knew, or should have known, that the clause was unfair. Deadlines in these cases are still argued in court, so do not wait: gather the loan documents and get advice early. Indicative period in Poland (contract claims): 3–6 years.

Sources:
- CJEU, Dziubak, case C-260/18: https://curia.europa.eu/juris/liste.jsf?num=C-260/18
- CJEU, Bank M., case C-520/21: https://curia.europa.eu/juris/liste.jsf?num=C-520/21
- Rzecznik Finansowy (Polish Financial Ombudsman): https://rf.gov.pl/

Q: Can I still sue mBank if I have repaid the Swiss franc loan?
A: Often yes. Borrowers who have repaid their loan have brought claims to recover what they overpaid, but the deadline question needs checking for your dates.

Q: Do lawyers take these cases on a success fee?
A: Many Polish firms offer a fixed fee plus a success fee, or a success fee only. Ask for the agreement in writing and how the fee is calculated if the bank settles.

Q: What did the CJEU decide about bank remuneration?
A: In June 2023 (case C-520/21) the Court held that, when a loan contract is annulled because of unfair terms, EU law precludes the bank from claiming compensation beyond the return of the capital and interest on it from when the payment was demanded.

### Claims against Mercedes-Benz: diesel emissions
URL: https://jurimatch.com/claims/mercedes-benz

Owners of some Mercedes-Benz diesel cars have brought claims arguing that emissions controls worked differently on the road than in tests, for example through temperature-dependent settings. German authorities ordered recalls of some models, and the manufacturer has disputed that its vehicles contained unlawful defeat devices. This guide explains how these claims have generally worked.

Damages for buyers in the EU: In March 2023 the Court of Justice of the EU ruled (case C-100/21, against Mercedes-Benz Group) that buyers can claim damages from a manufacturer that negligently installed an unlawful defeat device. Following that ruling, the German Federal Court of Justice (BGH) allowed damages for negligence, generally between 5% and 15% of the purchase price, depending on the case.

Group claims in England and Wales: Group claims over diesel emissions involving several manufacturers, Mercedes-Benz among them, have been brought in the High Court in London.

Which cars are affected: Claims depend on the specific engine, model and emissions class. A recall or software update letter is a useful starting point, but not every recalled car gives rise to a claim, and vice versa.

Deadlines: Limitation periods depend on the country, and the start date often depends on when buyers knew or should have known about the issue. Many claims about vehicles affected in 2015 have reached or passed the ordinary limit in some countries. Group actions have their own registration or opt-in deadlines. Use the limitation checker and ask a lawyer before assuming your claim is still open. Indicative period in Germany (non-contractual damages (tort)): 3 years (from knowledge).

Sources:
- CJEU, Mercedes-Benz Group, case C-100/21: https://curia.europa.eu/juris/liste.jsf?num=C-100/21

Q: Is my Mercedes affected?
A: It depends on the engine, model and emissions class. Recall letters and official vehicle checkers are a starting point; a lawyer or claims group can check your specific car.

Q: How much could I get?
A: There is no fixed amount. In Germany, courts following the 2023 CJEU ruling have generally awarded a percentage of the purchase price for negligence claims; elsewhere it depends on national law and the claim.

Q: Do lawyers take these cases on a no-win-no-fee basis?
A: Many do, often backed by litigation funding or legal expenses insurance. Ask how the fee is calculated and what happens if the claim fails.

### Claims against Norwegian: delays, cancellations and refunds
URL: https://jurimatch.com/claims/norwegian

Norwegian Air Shuttle is a Norwegian low-cost airline. Norway applies Regulation 261/2004 as part of the European Economic Area, so Norwegian's flights are covered in the same way as an EU airline's. Claims are mostly about delays, cancellations and refunds.

Delay and cancellation compensation: Under EU Regulation 261/2004 (and its UK copy, UK261), passengers can claim fixed compensation for long delays at arrival, late cancellations and denied boarding, unless the airline shows the disruption was caused by extraordinary circumstances such as severe weather or air traffic control restrictions. The amount depends on the flight distance.

Refunds and care: When a flight is cancelled, passengers are entitled to choose between a refund and re-routing, and to care (meals, and a hotel if an overnight stay is needed) while they wait. Customers have brought complaints where refunds were slow or only vouchers were offered.

Baggage: Lost, delayed or damaged luggage is covered by the Montreal Convention, which has short notice periods: report it at the airport and send a written claim to the airline quickly.

Deadlines: There is no single EU deadline for flight compensation: the limitation period is set by the law of the country where you bring the claim, and it varies considerably between countries. Baggage claims under the Montreal Convention have much shorter notice periods (days, not years) and a two-year limit for court action. Use the limitation checker for an indicative deadline in your country, and act early: evidence such as boarding passes and emails is easier to gather now. Indicative period in Norway (contract claims): 3 years.

Sources:
- Regulation (EC) No 261/2004 (EUR-Lex): https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2004/261/oj
- European Commission: national enforcement bodies under Regulation 261/2004: https://transport.ec.europa.eu/transport-themes/passenger-rights/national-enforcement-bodies-neb_en

Q: Do I need a lawyer to claim compensation from Norwegian?
A: Usually not for the first step: you can claim directly with the airline for free. A claim company or no-win-no-fee lawyer can help if the airline refuses or does not reply, in exchange for a share of the compensation.

Q: Does Norwegian have to pay if the delay was caused by weather or strikes?
A: Not if the disruption was caused by extraordinary circumstances that could not have been avoided with reasonable measures, such as severe weather. Courts have held that strikes by the airline's own staff are not normally extraordinary, while strikes by third parties such as air traffic controllers can be. Each case depends on its facts.

Q: How much compensation can I get?
A: Under EU261 the fixed amounts are 250, 400 or 600 euros depending on distance (UK261 uses pounds). Our flight compensation calculator shows which band applies. Refunds and expenses for care are separate from compensation.

### Claims against PKO Bank Polski: Swiss franc mortgages
URL: https://jurimatch.com/claims/pko-bp

PKO Bank Polski is Poland's largest bank. It is one of the banks that hold Swiss franc mortgage portfolios, and many borrowers have brought claims about the exchange-rate clauses in those loans. This guide explains how those claims generally work.

### Bad advice from a professional? Claiming for negligence
URL: https://jurimatch.com/claims/professional-negligence

Professionals owe a duty to act with reasonable skill and care. When they fall short and it causes a financial loss, you may have a claim, usually against their professional indemnity insurance.

Q: Who pays if I win a professional negligence claim?
A: Usually the professional's indemnity insurer, which is why these claims are often funded on success terms.

### Property and off-plan fraud: how to protect your claim
URL: https://jurimatch.com/claims/property-fraud

Property fraud ranges from fake listings and diverted deposits to off-plan developments that never complete and title problems discovered after purchase. Your contracts and payment records are the foundation of any claim.

Q: Can I recover a deposit from a developer that went bust?
A: Possibly, if your deposit was protected by a bank guarantee, escrow or insurance, or if directors can be held personally liable. Otherwise you may be an unsecured creditor in the insolvency.

Q: Do I need a lawyer in the country where the property is?
A: Usually yes, because property claims are generally governed by local law and heard by local courts.

### Claims against Renfe: train delays and refunds
URL: https://jurimatch.com/claims/renfe

Renfe is Spain's national rail operator, running AVE high-speed, long-distance and commuter trains. Its services are covered by the EU rail passenger rights rules, and Renfe also publishes its own punctuality commitment, which on some services is more generous than the EU minimum.

Delay compensation: Under Regulation (EU) 2021/782, which applies since June 2023, passengers can claim 25% of the ticket price for a delay at arrival of 60 to 119 minutes and 50% for 120 minutes or more, unless the delay was caused by extraordinary circumstances such as severe weather. Operators can set a minimum amount below which nothing is paid.

Refund or re-routing: If a delay of 60 minutes or more is expected, passengers can choose a refund, continuing the journey or re-routing, and are entitled to meals and, where needed, a hotel.

Deadlines: Regulation 2021/782 lets operators set a time limit for compensation requests, which cannot be shorter than three months after the journey. Ask for compensation as soon as possible. A court claim after that is subject to the general limitation rules of the country where you sue. Indicative period in Spain (contract claims): 5 years.

Sources:
- Regulation (EU) 2021/782 on rail passengers' rights (EUR-Lex): https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2021/782/oj

Q: How much does Renfe pay for a delay?
A: Under the EU minimum rules, 25% of the ticket price for 60 to 119 minutes late and 50% for 120 minutes or more. Some operators pay more under their own commitments; check the conditions of your ticket.

Q: Is a strike an extraordinary circumstance?
A: Regulation 2021/782 lists exceptions such as extreme weather and major natural disasters; strikes by the operator's own staff are not among them. Check the facts of your case.

### Romance and pig-butchering scams: what victims can do
URL: https://jurimatch.com/claims/romance-scam

Romance scams build trust over weeks or months, often before introducing an “investment” platform. Victims are not at fault, these are organised operations. There are practical steps that can still help.

Q: Will my bank refund a romance scam payment?
A: It depends on your country, how you paid and the bank's rules. Some countries have reimbursement schemes for authorised push-payment fraud. Report it to the bank immediately.

### Claims against Ryanair: delays, cancellations and refunds
URL: https://jurimatch.com/claims/ryanair

Ryanair is an Irish airline, so its flights from or to the EU are generally covered by EU Regulation 261/2004, and flights from the UK by UK261. Most passenger claims against it are about long delays, cancellations, refunds and baggage. This guide explains how those claims usually work.

Delay and cancellation compensation: Under EU Regulation 261/2004 (and its UK copy, UK261), passengers can claim fixed compensation for long delays at arrival, late cancellations and denied boarding, unless the airline shows the disruption was caused by extraordinary circumstances such as severe weather or air traffic control restrictions. The amount depends on the flight distance.

Refunds and care: When a flight is cancelled, passengers are entitled to choose between a refund and re-routing, and to care (meals, and a hotel if an overnight stay is needed) while they wait. Customers have brought complaints where refunds were slow or only vouchers were offered.

Baggage: Lost, delayed or damaged luggage is covered by the Montreal Convention, which has short notice periods: report it at the airport and send a written claim to the airline quickly.

Extra charges: Some passengers have brought complaints about fees for bags, seats or check-in. These are usually treated as consumer complaints rather than EU261 claims.

Deadlines: There is no single EU deadline for flight compensation: the limitation period is set by the law of the country where you bring the claim, and it varies considerably between countries. Baggage claims under the Montreal Convention have much shorter notice periods (days, not years) and a two-year limit for court action. Use the limitation checker for an indicative deadline in your country, and act early: evidence such as boarding passes and emails is easier to gather now. Indicative period in Ireland (contract claims): 6 years.

Sources:
- Regulation (EC) No 261/2004 (EUR-Lex): https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2004/261/oj
- UK261: Regulation 261/2004 as retained in UK law (legislation.gov.uk): https://www.legislation.gov.uk/eur/2004/261/contents

Q: Do I need a lawyer to claim compensation from Ryanair?
A: Usually not for the first step: you can claim directly with the airline for free. A claim company or no-win-no-fee lawyer can help if the airline refuses or does not reply, in exchange for a share of the compensation.

Q: Does Ryanair have to pay if the delay was caused by weather or strikes?
A: Not if the disruption was caused by extraordinary circumstances that could not have been avoided with reasonable measures, such as severe weather. Courts have held that strikes by the airline's own staff are not normally extraordinary, while strikes by third parties such as air traffic controllers can be. Each case depends on its facts.

Q: How much compensation can I get?
A: Under EU261 the fixed amounts are 250, 400 or 600 euros depending on distance (UK261 uses pounds). Our flight compensation calculator shows which band applies. Refunds and expenses for care are separate from compensation.

### Claims against Santander: mortgages, cards and Banco Popular
URL: https://jurimatch.com/claims/santander

Banco Santander is one of Spain's largest banks and acquired Banco Popular in 2017. Like other Spanish banks, it has faced consumer claims over mortgage terms and credit products, and former Banco Popular investors brought claims after Popular's 2017 resolution. This guide explains the usual claims and routes in Spain.

Floor clauses (cláusulas suelo): Mortgage terms that set a minimum interest rate. Since 2013 Spanish courts have held them void where they were not transparent, and since the CJEU's December 2016 ruling banks must repay everything charged under a void clause, with interest.

Mortgage set-up costs (gastos de hipoteca): Customers have claimed back part of the notary, registry, agency and valuation costs charged when the mortgage was signed, after courts held clauses passing all costs to the customer to be unfair.

Revolving credit cards: Claims that the interest rate was usurious or that the cost of the card was not explained clearly. The Supreme Court has ruled on how to compare revolving rates with the market average.

IRPH-indexed mortgages: Claims about mortgages indexed to IRPH instead of Euribor, where the question is whether the bank explained the index and its effect transparently.

Banco Popular shares and bonds: Banco Popular was resolved by the European authorities in June 2017 and sold to Santander. Shareholders and bondholders who lost their investment have brought claims, mainly arguing that they were misinformed when they bought. Outcomes have depended on when and how the investment was made.

Deadlines: In Spain, the Supreme Court and the Court of Justice of the European Union (CJEU) have held that the action to declare an unfair term void in a consumer contract does not expire. The time limit to recover money already paid is more debated: the CJEU has said it cannot start running before the consumer could know the term was unfair. Deadlines differ by product and are still developing through case law, so do not wait: get documents together and take advice early. Indicative period in Spain (contract claims): 5 years.

Sources:
- CJEU, Gutiérrez Naranjo, joined cases C-154/15, C-307/15 and C-308/15: https://curia.europa.eu/juris/liste.jsf?num=C-154/15
- CJEU, CaixaBank and BBVA, cases C-224/19 and C-259/19 (mortgage costs): https://curia.europa.eu/juris/liste.jsf?num=C-224/19
- Banco de España: Portal del Cliente Bancario: https://clientebancario.bde.es/

Q: Do I have to complain to Santander before going to court?
A: In practice, yes. A written complaint to the bank's customer service is required before you can go to the Banco de España complaints service, and since April 2025 most civil claims in Spain require a prior attempt to settle. A documented written complaint usually serves both purposes.

Q: Do lawyers take these cases on a no-win-no-fee basis?
A: Many do, especially floor clause and mortgage expense claims, because when the bank loses in full it is normally ordered to pay costs. Ask for the fee agreement (hoja de encargo) in writing, including what happens if the bank settles early.

Q: Can I still claim if I have paid off the loan?
A: Often yes. Having repaid or cancelled a mortgage does not by itself prevent a claim about an unfair term, but any later agreement or waiver you signed needs to be reviewed.

### Claims against Santander Bank Polska: Swiss franc mortgages
URL: https://jurimatch.com/claims/santander-bank-polska

Santander Bank Polska, formerly Bank Zachodni WBK, is part of the Santander group. Borrowers with Swiss franc mortgages from the bank and from banks it took over have brought claims about the exchange-rate clauses.

### Claims against SAS: delays, cancellations and refunds
URL: https://jurimatch.com/claims/sas

SAS (Scandinavian Airlines) is the airline of Denmark, Norway and Sweden, headquartered near Stockholm. Its flights are covered by Regulation 261/2004 when they depart from the EU or EEA, or fly into it. Claims are mostly about delays, cancellations, refunds and baggage.

### Claims against Scania: the trucks cartel
URL: https://jurimatch.com/claims/scania

Scania, the Swedish truck maker in the Traton group, did not settle with the European Commission and was fined separately in September 2017 for the same cartel. Its appeals were dismissed, and buyers of Scania trucks have claimed damages for the overcharge.

Damages for overcharges: In July 2016 the European Commission found that MAN, Volvo/Renault, Daimler, Iveco and DAF had colluded for 14 years (1997 to 2011) on truck pricing and on passing on the costs of emissions technology, and in September 2017 it found the same about Scania. Buyers and lessees of medium and heavy trucks from that period have claimed the extra price they paid.

Group claims: Many hauliers have joined group claims organised by law firms, associations or claim vehicles, often backed by litigation funders, in Spain, Germany, the Netherlands, the United Kingdom and elsewhere.

How the overcharge is proved: Claims rely on expert economic reports comparing cartel prices with the prices that would have applied without the cartel. Courts in several countries have estimated the damage when the evidence was incomplete.

Deadlines: In Volvo and DAF Trucks (C-267/20, June 2022) the CJEU held that the limitation period for these claims could not start before the Commission's decision was published in the EU Official Journal (April 2017 for the main decision), and applied the rules of the Damages Directive to many claims. Each country's limitation rules then apply, and some claims are already out of time. Check your dates with a lawyer before assuming your claim is open. Indicative period in Sweden (non-contractual damages (tort)): 10 years.

Sources:
- European Commission: Scania decision, September 2017: https://ec.europa.eu/commission/presscorner/detail/en/IP_17_3021
- CJEU, Volvo and DAF Trucks, case C-267/20 (limitation of cartel claims): https://curia.europa.eu/juris/liste.jsf?num=C-267/20
- Directive 2014/104/EU on competition damages actions (EUR-Lex): https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2014/104/oj

Q: Can my company still claim against Scania?
A: Possibly, depending on the country where you sue and when your limitation period started. After the CJEU's 2022 ruling many claims were filed, but each country's own rules decide whether yours is still open.

Q: Do I need the original invoices?
A: They help a lot. Where they are lost, registration records and bank statements can sometimes prove the purchase and its price.

Q: Who pays the expert report?
A: In group claims the funder or the law firm usually advances it and recovers it from the proceeds. In an individual claim, ask the firm how it is paid.

### Claims against SNCF Voyageurs: train delays and refunds
URL: https://jurimatch.com/claims/sncf

SNCF Voyageurs runs France's TGV INOUI, Ouigo, Intercités and regional trains. Its services are covered by the EU rail passenger rights rules, and SNCF also has its own delay guarantees on some services. Claims are mostly about delays, cancellations and strikes.

### Claims against SWISS: delays, cancellations and refunds
URL: https://jurimatch.com/claims/swiss

Swiss International Air Lines (SWISS) is Switzerland's national airline and part of the Lufthansa Group. Switzerland applies Regulation 261/2004 under its air transport agreement with the EU, so SWISS flights from Swiss and EU airports are covered in the same way as an EU airline's.
